### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: step 1.2
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "Suppose X is not Hausdorff. Choose distinct p,q for which every neighbourhood of p meets every neighbourhood of q, and let E = {(U,V,z): U∈N(p), V∈N(q), z∈U∩V}, ordered by reverse inclusion in the first two coordinates. [A1, construct]"
WHY IT FAILS: The citation of [A1] does not support the claim. [A1] states "Distinct points in a Hausdorff space have disjoint neighbourhoods." It makes no assertion about non‑Hausdorff spaces and does not justify the existence of such p,q. The existence follows from the negation of the definition of Hausdorff (a dependency of the page) but not from [A1]. The step itself is mathematically correct; the citation is erroneous.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Replace "[A1, construct]" by a reference to the definition of Hausdorff, or remove the reference to A1 (the step is adequately described by "construct" together with the definition).

### FINDING 2 — NONFATAL — location: step 2.2
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "The set E is directed: intersect the first two neighbourhood coordinates of two triples and choose a point in their intersection; the resulting triple is above both. The net sending (U,V,z) to z is eventually in every neighbourhood of p and every neighbourhood of q, hence converges to both distinct points. [step 1.2, A1, A2]"
WHY IT FAILS: The citation of [A1] is again misplaced. [A1] concerns Hausdorff spaces and does not help to prove that the net converges in the (non‑Hausdorff) contrapositive branch. The step is properly justified by step 1.2 and [A2]; [A1] is irrelevant and constitutes a citation of an item for a claim it does not make. The logical validity of the step is unaffected.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Remove "[A1]" from the justification; "[step 1.2, A2]" (or simply "[step 1.2]") is sufficient.
